name: Marginal Papular Palmoplantar Keratoderma
aliases: Marginal Papular Keratoderma of the Palms and Soles

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Marginal Papular Palmoplantar Keratoderma Diagnostic Criteria

criteria.description: Presence of papular hyperkeratotic lesions localized to the margins of the palms and soles
Skin biopsy showing hyperkeratosis with acanthosis and absence of epidermolytic changes
Positive family history consistent with autosomal dominant inheritance

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of characteristic marginal papular keratoderma lesions confirmed by histopathology
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing may be inconclusive; diagnosis primarily clinical and histological

laboratory: Skin biopsy showing hyperkeratosis and acanthosis without epidermolytic changes
genetic: Possible mutations in keratin genes (e.g., KRT1, KRT9) though not consistently identified
other: Clinical examination revealing characteristic marginal papular lesions

distinguishingFeatures: Punctate keratotic lesions diffusely distributed rather than marginal
Linear hyperkeratotic lesions along palmar creases

redFlags: Rapid progression of lesions with ulceration
Signs of secondary infection (e.g., purulence, increased erythema)
Development of systemic symptoms such as fever or malaise
references: Fischer J, et al. Palmoplantar keratodermas: clinical and molecular classification. Am J Med Genet C Semin Med Genet. 2006.
